name: kvserve
task: A key-value server over TCP speaking kvd's line protocol (GET, SET, INCR, DEL), every change appended to a write-ahead log of CRC-32 framed records in kvd's format before it is answered, with no sync (`--sync never`), the store in memory behind a reader-writer lock and the log behind a mutex (README.md).

hand.rust: a CRC-32 (IEEE, the reflected polynomial 0xEDB88320) with its 256-entry table built at start, about 25 lines: Rust's std has no CRC; everything else is std's

skip.c: no std sockets (C's std has none), as the http row

models.mk: tasks (std.net, one task per connection, MK_CARRIERS=8)
models.rust: OS threads (std::net, one std::thread per connection)
models.zig: OS threads (std.Io.net, one Io.Group.concurrent thread per connection)

unsafe_why: src/snap maps a snapshot with fs.Map in an unsafe block, at recovery only. The row never reaches it: every server starts on an empty data directory, so recovery finds no snapshot (snap.Load returns before MapOwn), and `--compact-after 1000000000` keeps the server from writing one during a run.
notes: The Mk side is Dogfoods/kvd unchanged (D-844): `kvd serve`, with two of its own flags after the common command line: `--compact-after 1000000000`, so it never compacts during a run (its default compacts every 1,000 changes, which the twins do not do), and `--max-clients 10000`, above the row's connections and tools/bench's probe connection (its default is 1,000).

The load is tools/bench's kv generator (kvbench.go): each connection owns 64 keys, half text and half counters, and draws from splitmix(seed + i) GET 50%, SET 25% (8 to 64 bytes of letters, digits and inner spaces), INCR 15% and DEL 10%; every reply is checked against the connection's model. After each server stops, tools/bench reads its log: a fresh header, every record's CRC-32, one record per answered change, and the replayed store equal to the connections' models.
Connections close with a reset (linger 0), as the http row's; 256 connections hold 512 sockets at once, below the owner's 10,000 cap.
